column2: You, O Agni, are the priest of all sacrifices, placed among the gods for the people of men.
We choose Agni as messenger, the priest who knows all things, the one skilled in this sacrifice.
Agni, kindled, bright and well-fed with offerings, strikes down obstacles; seeking wealth, he is praised with devotion.
I praise your dearest guest, beloved like a friend — Agni, who is to be known like a chariot.
O Agni, protect us with your mighty powers from every enemy, and from the mortal who hates us.
Come, let me speak to you, Agni, other words as well; grow strong through these soma-drops.
Your calf has turned its mind to you from the farthest dwelling; O Agni, I long for you with my song.
O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the lotus leaf, from the head of the whole bearer of offerings.
O Agni, bring to us radiant gifts for our great protection; for you are a god, to be seen by us.
Homage to your might, O Agni; the peoples sing to you, O god. Crush our enemies with your strength.
With song I adorn your messenger, the knower of all, the immortal bearer of offerings, the best of sacrificers.
The hymns of the offering-makers approach you like sisters, pointing the way; they have stood before the wind.
O Agni, day by day, morning and evening, with devout thought we come to you bearing homage.
Awake the worshipful one; enter each clan for the sake of him who deserves worship — a pleasing hymn to Rudra.
You are invoked to this lovely sacrifice to drink the soma; come, Agni, with the Maruts.
I praise you, Agni, like a horse with its mane, with homage — the sovereign of sacrifices.
I call the pure Agni, clothed in the sea, as the Aurva and the Bhrigus did.
Kindling Agni with the mind, let the mortal gain insight; I kindle Agni together with the Vivasvans.
They behold the light of the ancient seed, the day, when it is kindled high in heaven.
We invoke Agni, who increases the sacrifices and is most abundant, for the strong grandson.
Agni, with his sharp flame, subdues every devourer; may Agni bring wealth to us.
O Agni, be gracious; you are great. You have come to the people devoted to the gods, to sit on the sacred grass.
O Agni, protect us from distress; burn the harmful, O god, with your hottest flames, unaging one.
O Agni, yoke your horses, god — the good, swift ones that carry you well.
O lord of the people, we meditate upon you, the radiant, rich in heroes; O Agni who receives the oblation.
Agni is the head and summit of heaven, the lord of the earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Agni, speak among the gods for this our new Gayatri hymn, our offering of praise.
Gopavana praised you with song, O Agni Angiras; O purifier, hear our call.
Agni, lord of strength and seer, has gone around the offerings, bestowing treasures on the giver.
His rays carry aloft the god Jatavedas, that all may see the Sun.
Praise Agni the seer at the sacrifice — the god who keeps truth and drives away disease.
May the divine waters be good for us, for our desire; may they be good for drinking; may they flow around us with health and blessing.
Whom do you now surround, lord of the good; whose thoughts do you quicken? Whose songs do you accept?
At every sacrifice and with every song we honor Agni for his skill; let me praise the immortal Jatavedas, dear like a friend.
Protect us, Agni, with one verse, protect us with a second; protect us with three songs, lord of strength, protect us with four, O Vasu.
O Agni, with your great flames and bright radiance, O god, kindled among the Bharadvajas, shine richly, O youngest, O purifier.
O Agni of the good offering, may your patrons be dear to you, the liberal lords who give wide pastures of cattle to the people.
O Agni, praised by your worshipper, lord of the clans, burning the demons, O god, never absent, lord of the house, you are great, protector of heaven, dwelling in our homes.
O Agni, immortal, bring bright wondrous wealth with the dawn; carry the gods who wake with the dawn to the giver today.
O wondrous one, O Vasu, urge on riches with your help; you, Agni, are the charioteer of this wealth; find for us a shallow ford for our offspring.
Agni, protector, you alone are wide and true, a seer; the wise, kindling you, bright one, serve you, the ordainers.
O purifying Agni, bring us wealth that increases vigor and is worthy of praise; grant us, O nearest friend, wealth much desired, with good guidance and great fame.
Whoever grants all treasures, the joyful priest of the peoples — to him first let our hymns go forth like cups of honey, to Agni.
I invoke Agni with this homage, the grandson of strength, beloved, most attentive, ever near, with a fair sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
You lie in the forests and in your mothers; mortals kindle you. Untiring, you carry the offering for the giver, and then you reign among the gods.
He has been seen, the best knower of the way, in whom the sacred rites are placed; may our songs reach Agni, the newborn increaser of the Aryan.
Agni is set forward in the hymn; the pressing-stones are at the sacrifice, the grass is spread; with the verse I come to the Maruts and Brahmanaspati — the gods' protection is to be chosen.
Praise Agni for your protection with songs, him of the burning flame; O Agni, bountiful, famed among men, grant us wealth; Agni gives shelter for brilliant light.
Hear us, O Agni with listening ear, with the gods who come in company; may Mitra and Aryaman sit on the grass at the early-morning sacrifice with those who come at dawn.
Agni, the god, son of Divodasa, like Indra in might, has gone forth; he moves after his mother Earth and stands in the shelter of heaven.
Now from the earth, or from the great shining heaven, grow with this body and this song of mine; O skilful one, fulfill my offspring.
When, desiring the woods, you went to the waters, your mothers, O Agni, that return of yours is not forgotten, even though you were far away.
Manu set you, Agni, as light for the eternal people; you shine, born of truth and sprinkled, whom the peoples worship — Kanva.
May the god, giver of wealth, bring you the full pouring-vessel; pour it out or fill it up — then the god carries it on to you.
May Brahmanaspati go forth; may divine Truth go forth; may the gods lead our sacrifice to a hero, a leader, who gives abundant wealth.
Stand up for our help like the god Savitar; standing high, the winner of strength, whom we invoke with hymns and with the offering priests.
The mortal who, O Vasu, wishes to bring wealth and gives to you, gains a hero by himself, one who praises, who nourishes thousands.
We choose Agni, great among many peoples who seek the gods, with well-spoken words; whom others also kindle together.
This Agni rules over heroic strength and good fortune; he rules over wealth and good offspring; he rules over cattle and the slayings of Vritra.
You, Agni, are the lord of the house; you are our priest at the sacrifice; you are the Potri, O all-choosing, wise one; you give desirable things and go to them.
We, your friends, have chosen you, god, for help — the son of the waters, fortunate, skilful, swift to act, unfailing.
Pour the oblation and cleanse him; set the priest, the lord of the house, in his place; with homage worship at the altar the worshipful one of the peoples, to whom the offering is given.
Wondrous is the youth who, like a young child, does not follow his two mothers to be suckled; when he, though not milk-fed, was born, he immediately carries on, performing a great messenger's task.
This is one form of yours; another is beyond; enter into a third light. May your entry be a delight for your body; be dear to the gods in the highest birthplace.
We fashion this hymn for the worthy Jatavedas with our mind, as we fashion a chariot; his favor is good for us; in your friendship, Agni, may we not come to harm.
The head of heaven, the lord of earth, Vaishvanara, Agni born in the order of truth; the seer, sovereign, guest of men — the gods who sat near made him their cup.
Like waters from the mountain's back, O Agni, the gods bring you forth with hymns; the well-praised songs urge you on like horses winning in a race, O you who are borne by songs.
Make for your protection Agni, king of the sacrifice, Rudra, the priest true in sacrifice for heaven and earth, golden-formed, before the thunder's unexpected stroke.
The king is kindled with homage, whose face is anointed with ghee; men with offerings praise him, together in need; Agni has shone first among the dawns.
Agni goes forth with a great banner; the bull roars to heaven and earth; he has reached the nearest end of heaven; the mighty one has grown in the lap of the waters.
